findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh:2583 (13j writer) and :2651 (13k writer) — the bd-write arm of the same poll R3-F1 part (a) repaired
findings.evidence: R3-F1 IS COMPREHENSIVELY FIXED AND I PROVED IT WITH MY OWN FORCED-EXPIRY MUTANT, so this is a sibling residual, not a re-open. THE FIX, VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: I built a mutant on a scratchpad COPY replacing `            _POLL_DS=$(( 80 + (EXPECTED - 1) * 3 + 50 ))` with `_POLL_DS=1` (POLL_MAX_ITERS=(1+1)/2=1 -> a 0.2s bound), with all four non-vacuity proofs — target line found EXACTLY once (python count), mutant differs from shipped (cmp), parses (bash -n rc=0), old formula 0 lines in mutant / 1 line in shipped and new value 1 line in mutant. Run: rc=1, Total 446, FAILED 11, wall 574s. THE SENTINEL REACHES THE PARENT AND FAILS THE RUN, NAMED AND FIRST: `FAIL: 13j.pre2` at log line 330 precedes `FAIL: 13j.2` at 334, and `FAIL: 13k.pre2` at 386 precedes `FAIL: 13k.1` at 389; 13j.pre2 reads `expected: no / actual: yes`; both pre2 legs appear by name in the trailing failed-tests list. So the file-based channel out of the background subshell is real, not assumed. AND R3'S MISATTRIBUTION SYMPTOM IS ELIMINATED RATHER THAN RENAMED: grepping the mutant's whole 13j/13k region for the r3 signature `stub-0*(6[0-9]|7[0-2])\.sh` returns NOTHING (r3 observed stub-065.sh and stub-069.sh named where zz-slow-clean.sh was expected); the shipped runs A and B name only `zz-slow-clean.sh`. The write is SKIPPED, so no wrong spec is named at all. THE RESIDUAL: the OTHER premise of the same leg is still unasserted. Both writers run `cd "$FX_EXTERNAL" && bd comment "$EXT_TARGET" ... >/dev/null 2>&1` (and `bd label add` in 13k) with the exit status discarded and no `||` arm — I grepped both writer blocks and neither captures rc. So if the poll SUCCEEDS but the bd write then fails (store lock contention, a transient dolt error), no sentinel is written, 13j.pre2 passes, and 13j.2/13j.4-13j.7 fail as a cluster with no named premise — the exact confusing shape R3-F1 part (a) was filed to close, reached by the other arm of the same `if`.
findings.description: NOT BLOCKING and I want the reason on the record rather than implied: it is strictly milder than R3-F1 was. A failed write produces no store movement, so the downstream failures say 'nothing was degraded' rather than misattributing to an unrelated stub — bounded and honest, just unexplained. It is also lower-probability: 13j.pre already asserts bd worked at fixture-build time, so this needs a LATER transient failure. I am recording it because this batch's whole thesis is that a reporting channel which can silently drop is the defect family, and this is one, in the leg that just had its twin closed. SUGGESTED FIX, symmetric with the one that landed and about four lines: `bd comment ... || : > "$EXT_WRITE_FAILED_MARK"`, plus a 13j.pre3/13k.pre3 precondition asserting the mark is absent, worded like pre2. Worth folding into dhh7 rather than spawning a task.

findings.location: claude-workflow-plugin-k0mc (open P1 bug) observed live this cycle; plus the overstated re-arm claim at .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh:6586-6587
findings.evidence: I MEASURED THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN CITING IT. `sort -u .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-16` = `fd30f3a1078af7ed` — identical to the change_set_hash the gate bound at enter and to the request's own change_set_hash, which proves directly that change_set_hash is the digest of the sorted PATH LIST and is content-blind. THIS BIT, LIVE, DURING THIS REVIEW. I entered the gate at 20:49:52. The dhh7 implementer — spawned at 13:39:07Z (20:39 local) per .claude/.qa-tracking/subagent-spawns.log, ten minutes BEFORE my own qa spawn at 13:49:16Z — then rewrote run-tests.sh at 20:51:07 and runner-completeness.test.sh at 21:03:38 (stat mtimes; .qa-tracking/changed-files.txt and edit-count share the 21:03:38 mtime, so post-edit.sh fired, i.e. these were agent Write/Edit calls, not filesystem noise), and recorded its completion contract at 21:16. I detected this independently at 21:05 when a `grep -nF 'LEGACY MODE'` returned a hit at line 4114 where a `sed -n '4080,4115p'` eight minutes earlier had shown section 20 — then confirmed it by mtime. ACROSS ALL OF IT change_set_hash NEVER MOVED: I measured fd30f3a1... at 20:49 and again at 21:33 and at 21:59, identical every time. An approval written at 21:00 would have bound fd30f3a1 and certified bytes that changed three minutes later, with nothing in the gate able to notice. THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNOWS THIS AND HAS IT FILED: k0mc is an OPEN P1 bug named 'approve truncates the tracker...', whose own comment records the identical signature from a9hh ('content moves, hash does not, so an approval attests to bytes nobody read: five files rewritten between rounds, hash identical') and a second instance from rqer. verify-before-stop.sh DOES have a content-sensitive instrument, `tree_fingerprint()` (line 719), and its header at :3146-3178 states this blind spot explicitly — but I traced its call sites and it gates the VERIFIED-STATE-UNCHANGED / skip decision at :3362, NOT the approval binding. The approval predicate (:6580-6587) matches on change_set_hash alone. WHAT THE DEADLINE SAYS: k0mc carries an OPERATOR DIRECTIVE dated 2026-08-13 — 'NOT a D2 blocker, but DECIDE THE MECHANISM NOW and land the migration BEFORE D5' — and the decision was already taken in that comment ('UNIFY ON D1'S MECHANISM — a content hash that refuses before hashing'). HEAD is b372d6d, 'feat(fkm.8 D6)', with D5 (fkm.7) already landed in 0c3106b/6de6c9e/0dfb82a. So D5 and D6 both shipped with the migration undone and the directive's deadline passed.
findings.description: NOT A DEFECT IN THIS CHANGE SET and NOT grounds to block it — k0mc predates this batch, a P1 task owns it, and blocking gytz would hold four verified-correct fixes hostage to an unrelated open bug. I am recording it because I was asked whether the batch is ready to commit, and the honest answer has to name that this batch's own approval will bind a path-list hash over a change set whose contents provably moved mid-review. TWO CONCRETE, CHEAP ASKS, neither of which is k0mc's full migration. (1) The prose at verify-before-stop.sh:6586-6587 says condition (2) 're-arms the gate after any post-approval edit'. That is OVERSTATED in exactly the direction k0mc is about: it re-arms only when the PATH LIST moves, so an edit to a file already in the tracked set — the common case, and precisely what happened twice today — does not re-arm it. One qualifying clause there, in the same voice the :3146-3178 header already uses, stops a future auditor concluding the case is covered. (2) For THIS batch, the operator already has the right instrument and used it: `git status --porcelain | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-16`. I reproduced the coordinator's stated `8980f8b6787ee713` exactly, and re-measured it unchanged at 21:33 and 21:59. Re-taking that one value immediately before the acceptance run, and again before commit, costs one command and closes this window for this batch without waiting on k0mc.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh:2566-2570 (the 13j 'Background writer' comment), read against the new derivation comment 87 lines above it at :2479-2526
findings.evidence: The comment still reads: 'The poll carries the wall-clock bound LESSONS.md:282 requires (60 * 0.2s = 12s) — a single bound is enough here ... and giving up after 12s fails the assertions below loudly rather than hanging.' BOTH CLAUSES ARE NOW FALSE, and I verified each against the code rather than by eye. (1) The literal 60 no longer exists: the bound is `POLL_MAX_ITERS=$(( (_POLL_DS + 1) / 2 ))` over `_POLL_DS=$(( 80 + (EXPECTED - 1) * 3 + 50 ))`. I recomputed it independently — 80 + 71*3 + 50 = 343 deciseconds, (343+1)//2 = 172 iterations, 172 * 0.2s = 34.4s — which reproduces the derivation comment's own stated 34.4s exactly, and is 2.87x the 12s this stale paragraph claims. (2) Giving up no longer 'fails the assertions below': that is precisely what R3-F1 part (a) changed, and my mutant proves it — on expiry the writer now SKIPS the write and drops a sentinel, and the named 13j.pre2 fires FIRST. The same paragraph is also the one that documents the timing lesson, so a reader sizing this bound in future lands on the wrong number in the file's own audit trail. 13k carries no equivalent stale figure (its comment is a back-reference to 13j with no number), so this is one location, not two.
findings.description: Documentation drift, non-blocking, and identical in class to R3-F3 — which THIS ROUND fixed correctly in two other places, with an explicit CORRECTED note in each. What makes it worth a line rather than silence is position: it sits 87 lines below the new derivation block that contradicts it, inside the very `if` the fix rewrote, in a file whose headers are its audit trail. FIX: replace the parenthetical with the derived form (`POLL_MAX_ITERS, derived from $EXPECTED — 34.4s at EXPECTED=72; see the derivation block above`) and replace 'fails the assertions below loudly' with 'fails 13j.pre2 by name and skips the write'.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh:2833-2835 — the LEGACY MODE caveat text added for R3-F2
findings.evidence: R3-F2 IS FIXED AND THE PAIRING IS GENUINE. The identity diff (DISCOVERED_BASENAMES / DECLARED_BASENAMES / two-way `comm`) is now computed UNCONDITIONALLY before either branch decides anything; only the gating depends on EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT_ON. The new caveat is a SEPARATE printf after the existing HELD line, so no pre-existing assertion on that line's verbatim text is disturbed — a deliberate and correct choice. The implementer also read r3's measured CONVENTION rather than r3's suggested wording: the caveat fires only when legacy mode actually let a mismatch through (STRICT_ON=0 AND SET_MISMATCH=1), never merely to announce the mode, which is what 'announce when the weaker mode lets something through' actually requires and is what STRICT_SECTIONS does. A full four-leg pairing landed at section 19f (11 assertions: 19f.a1-a3 restore control on an exact-match fixture with NO caveat, 19f.b1-b5 the rename fixture WITH the caveat named, 19f.c1-c3 strict mode over the identical fixture never reaching HELD at all) — and 19f.a correctly builds its OWN fixture via the new mk_l1_fixture_named/L1_REAL_SPEC_NAMES rather than reusing FX_MANIFEST, whose count 19b had permanently moved to 73. All 11 legs pass in both my runs. THE NIT: the caveat's first line says 'the spec-set IDENTITY was not checked this run', and the very next clause says 'and it does not actually match EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES' — which is knowable only BECAUSE it was checked. After this fix the identity IS computed on every run; what STRICT_ON=0 drops is ENFORCEMENT, not the check.
findings.description: Non-blocking and the error is in the SAFE direction — the reader is told plainly that the names do not agree and not to read HELD as a claim that they do, so nobody is misled about the state of the world. It is worth one word because this batch is specifically about claims that misdescribe what was verified, and here the claim UNDERSTATES it while the code does more than it says. FIX: 'was not ENFORCED this run' (or 'was checked but not enforced'). Leg 19f.b4's needle is the substring 'spec-set IDENTITY was not', which survives that edit unchanged.

findings.location: the two inherited-figure corrections I was asked to verify rather than accept, plus the coordinator's own host figures
findings.evidence: CORRECTION 1 — 'one dolt hashof per spec plus one at arm, NOT two per spec as r3 stated' — VERIFIED CORRECT BY DIRECT READING. `grep -n hashof run-tests.sh` gives 9 LINES THAT MENTION it, of which exactly TWO are executions: :1985 in the ARM block and :2425 inside the per-spec loop opened at `for test_file in "${TESTS[@]}"` at :2274. The comment at :2421-2422 states the model ('40 hashof calls across a 39-spec tier, not 78: one at arm time, one per spec thereafter') and the code matches it, because STORE_HASH_BEFORE is reassigned at the bottom of the block and carries the previous spec's 'after' forward. So r3's DIAGNOSIS stands and r3's NUMBER does not — exactly as the coordinator reported, and I confirm it against the code rather than against the report. CORRECTION 2 — 'verify_actor_marker_took_effect costs ~5s, not the ~2.5-2.8s the shipped comment claimed' — VERIFIED, WITH MY OWN NUMBERS AND ONE HONEST DISAGREEMENT ON MAGNITUDE. So the old '~2.5-2.8s' is the init-only cost almost exactly, and the correction's DIRECTION is right — the shipped comment understated its own function by roughly 1.66x. WHERE I DIFFER FROM THE CORRECTED TEXT: run-tests.sh:1860-1862 now states 'the real ~5-5.6s figure', and my quiet-host measurement is 4.74-4.83s, BELOW that range (the implementer measured 5.25/4.88/5.61 under heavier load).
